AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To assess the outcomes for patients with chronic idiopathic pelvic pain (CIPP) and associated pelvic floor disorders (PFDs) undergoing laparoscopic ventral mesh rectopexy (LVMR).

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: A prospective database identified patients referred from a specialist pain clinic undergoing LVMR. Primary outcomes included numerical rating scale (NRS) for pain, quality of life (QoL), Wexner constipation score, Cleveland Clinic incontinence score (CCIS), bowel and bladder-disturbance visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score and sexual function. 30-day mortality, morbidity, mesh related complications, recurrence and further treatment were evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Seventy-five patients were identified. Median age was 54 (18-82) years with a median follow-up of 17 (IQR 11-28) months. NRS decreased from a median of 9 (IQR 8-10) to 3.5 (IQR 1-5, P < 0.0001). QoL (Birmingham Bowel & Urinary Symptoms Questionnaire - 22) improved at 3 months (57 vs 34, P < 0.0001) and was sustained at 36 months (57 vs 33, P = 0.001). Wexner constipation score and CCIS both reduced at 3 months (P < 0.0001) and (P < 0.0001) respectively. The bladder and bowel-symptom severity VAS scores decreased and were maintained at 36 months (P = 0.0234) and (P = 0.002). Dyspareunia improved in 94% (n = 50). 30-day complication rate was 18% (n = 13) with no mortality and 4% (n = 3) had mesh related complications requiring reoperation. 13% (n = 10) of patients developed recurrence of symptoms and 8% (n = 6) of patients required further specialist pain management.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: For patients labelled with CIPP, treating associated PFDs, using LVMR, significantly reduces pain and improves QoL, which is maintained. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
